I've been working this land for 45 years. I know what Quzhou's soil and weather demand. My well gives me water when the rains don't cooperate, and that's kept me steady. Two of us in the house now — I can't take on more than I can manage with my own hands and maybe some hired help at cotton harvest.

**Cotton (my main crop — 4 mu):** Cotton is what I've built my income on. I'll put 4 mu into it, same as last few years. I'll plough deep in April before transplanting — I've always done it that way, the roots need room. I'll use the improved seed from the county extension station, not the new hybrid varieties — too expensive and I'm not sure they suit my fields. Cotton in this heat needs water at five key stages: before planting, seedling time, budding, flowering/bolling, and once more as bolls set. Bollworm and aphids are always a problem here so I'll spray seven times through the season. I expect around 280 jin per mu of seed cotton if the weather holds.

**Wheat (3 mu, winter):** After I pull the maize in September, I'll rotary-till those 3 mu and sow wheat in October. I split my urea — some at sowing, the rest at jointing. I irrigate four times: a good soaking before sowing, once before it goes dormant, again at jointing, and once at heading. Two pesticide passes keep the rust and aphids off. I've gotten 450 jin per mu consistently on these fields.

**Maize (3 mu, summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I seed maize directly into the stubble — no tillage, saves time and the soil stays moist. I use hybrid seed, everyone does now and the yield difference is real. Three irrigations — at planting, jointing, and silking. Two pesticide sprays. I expect 550 jin per mu.
